- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect mean reversion or rebound potential.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overreacts with continued steep rise; cap forecast slope or introduce lagged correction.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; add a “sentiment pivot” trigger to adjust forecast mid-series.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply a “late-period bias” correction: add 1–2% to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.00 or 0.33), model tends to underestimate; apply a “sentiment decay” rule: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment remains below 0.67 for 3+ days.
